title: Oldest known terrestrial zircon, Jack Hills (4.404 Ga)
summary: Ion-microprobe uranium-lead dating of detrital zircon grain W74/2-36 from metamorphosed conglomerate at Jack Hills, Western Australia, established an age of 4,404 ± 8 million years. Enriched oxygen isotope ratios in this crystal demonstrated that continental crust and liquid surface water existed within 160 million years of Earth's formation, refuting earlier models of a dry, uniformly molten Hadean surface.

uncertainty.note: 2-sigma analytical uncertainty from ion microprobe U-Pb isotopic analysis on grain W74/2-36 (Wilde et al. 2001).

where.modern_name: Erawondoo Hill, Jack Hills, Western Australia, Australia
where.historical_name: Hadean protocrust, prior to any named cratonic or plate configurations

importance.justification: Detrital zircon grain W74/2-36 from Jack Hills is the oldest dated mineral grain discovered on Earth, providing geochemical evidence that liquid water and differentiated crust formed during the Hadean eon.

related.because: Planetary accretion and early differentiation produced the protocrust in which the Hadean zircons crystallized.

sources.title: Evidence from detrital zircons for the existence of continental crust and oceans on the Earth 4.4 Gyr ago (Nature 409:175–178)
